title: Why Busan's Colorful Hillside Village Looks Like This
mediaSource: Busan Gamcheon Culture Village refugee settlement hillside urban regeneration

scenes.title: Why do these Busan houses climb the hill like stairs?
scenes.narration: Gamcheon Culture Village is famous for its colors today, but it began as a home for people displaced by the Korean War.

scenes.title: Refugees and a religious community settled here in the 1950s
scenes.narration: After the war, displaced families and members of the Taegeukdo community moved into Gamcheon and built densely along the hillside.

scenes.title: Steep terrain shaped the houses and alleys
scenes.narration: With little flat land, homes rose in terraces while narrow winding stairways connected the neighborhood.

scenes.title: Art projects arrived in 2009
scenes.narration: A village art project added public artworks and color, followed by community-based urban regeneration efforts.

scenes.title: People still live here
scenes.narration: Despite its fame as a tourist destination, Gamcheon remains a real residential neighborhood where visitors are asked to respect local life.

scenes.title: The colors came later than the history
scenes.narration: Gamcheon's unique cityscape was shaped first by displacement and settlement, and later by art and urban regeneration.
